interpretation: The 14297204736 byte field comes from torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated at capture_end. It is not the 13758924800-byte reconstructed allocation-history peak or a lower bound inferred from that reconstruction.

peak_is_exact=false denotes incomplete allocator-history reconstruction (ring capacity200000 and unmatched prefix), not a missing numeric CUDA counter. The existing report intentionally retains that conservative flag and withholds its exact-peak reduction display.

The selected target is fix-oom: its memory condition is original OOM plus a valid completed20-update candidate. Standard numerical, parameter, measured-CUDA and GPU checks remain required; no fit ceiling is proved from incomplete reconstruction.

The 42.2 percent figure is arithmetic between recorded original-OOM and candidate CUDA counters. It does not estimate the memory needed to finish the original workload and is not a full-baseline reduction guarantee.
The numerical basis is first five backward scalar losses against a baseline-derived checkpoint-transformed reference. No full20-scalar equivalence is claimed.

The old report label table did not recognize this checkpoint numerical basis, independently explaining Comparison basis not recorded in presentation. No raw result, peak flag or acceptance rule was edited by this review.
